title: STY/DOC: implement UP (pyupgrade) suggestions to doc/tutorials
body:
Modernise the tutorial scripts a bit, using the ruff UP (pyupgrade) rules. These are enabled in pyproject.toml but just for those files: if we apply this to more files the `per-file-ignores` can be updated.

It would be a good idea for a reviewer to try running the updated tutorials, I'm not sure if they run in CI?

# Checklist: `x` (done) or `~` (irrelevant)

- [X] [I am familiar with **ASE's contribution guidelines.**](https://ase-lib.org/development/contribute.html)
- [~] [**Doc strings** in code changed in this MR are up to date.](https://ase-lib.org/development/python_codingstandard.html#writing-documentation-in-the-code)
- [~] [**Unit tests** have been added for new or changed code.](https://ase-lib.org/development/tests.html)
- [~] [**Changes** have been added in `changelog.d` using `scriv`.](https://ase-lib.org/development/writing_changelog.html)
- [~] [**Issue is resolved** via "closes #XXXX" if applicable.](https://docs.gitlab.com/ee/user/project/issues/managing_issues.html#closing-issues-automatically)
author: ajjackson

comments.author: yuzie007
comments.body:
This looks a fancy update for ASE styling!

I ran the updated scripts manually.
There are no errors related to the style update itself, while I found the following:

1. For `ga_bulk_relax.py`
```
% python ga_bulk_run.py
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/Users/ikeda/codes/ase/doc/tutorials/ga/ga_bulk_run.py", line 1, in <module>
    from ga_bulk_relax import relax
  File "/Users/ikeda/codes/ase/doc/tutorials/ga/ga_bulk_relax.py", line 3, in <module>
    from ase.constraints import ExpCellFilter
ImportError: cannot import name 'ExpCellFilter' from 'ase.constraints' (/Users/ikeda/codes/ase/ase/constraints.py)
```
where we should update as
```
from ase.filters import ExpCellFilter
```

2. Since !3733, [this line in `ga_bulk_relax.py`](https://gitlab.com/ase/ase/-/blob/b448a2f091f6a02bfe8cfd52816769696722acae/doc/tutorials/ga/ga_bulk_relax.py#L49) does not work. `maxmove` should also be updated as `maxstep`.
So, we need to modify this part e.g. as
```python
        ecf = ExpCellFilter(atoms)
        dyn = FIRE(ecf, maxstep=0.2, logfile=None, trajectory=None)
        dyn.run(fmax=1e-3, steps=100)

        converged = dyn.converged(ecf.get_forces().ravel())
        niter += 1
```

3. `md/moldyn4.py` shows the following error
```
AttributeError: 'MPI' object has no attribute 'sum_scalar'
```
which is probably because Asap3 MPI does not have `sum_scalar`.
For a quick fix, we can do
```python
use_asap = False
```

These also show that the tutorial scripts are not tested on pipelines.
It would be ideal in future to auto-test these somehow like other `*.py` in `doc` via `ase/utils/sphinx.py`, but I am not immediately sure how:)

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: The comment identifies multiple concrete bugs and suggests specific code fixes: updating the import from ase.constraints to ase.filters, changing maxmove to maxstep in ga_bulk_relax.py, and setting use_asap=False in moldyn4.py.

comments.author: askhl
comments.body:
Very good idea to use pyupgrade.

We are extracting `ase.ga` to a separate project, so those tutorials will go elsewhere.  It would nevertheless be a Good Thing if asap had the same MPI interface.  @schiotz do you think we could get `comm.sum_scalar()` in asap?  GPAW implements it.

comments.author: schiotz
comments.body:
> do you think we could get `comm.sum_scalar()` in asap? GPAW implements it.

In my opinion, the MPI interface of GPAW and Asap should be as identical as possible.  Asap issue number 73.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: The comment requests that asap implement comm.sum_scalar() to match GPAW's MPI interface, directed at a specific person (@schiotz).

comments.author: ajjackson
comments.body: Great! I'll apply Yuji's suggestions then invite people to re-review/merge.

comments.author: ajjackson
comments.body:
```        converged = dyn.converged(ecf.get_forces().ravel())```

As raised in #1744 , this was not a very user-friendly change and in this case makes the tutorial code a bit mysterious. 

Looking more closely at `run`/`irun`, it returns True if convergence was reached.

So we can combine the lines into
```python
        converged = dyn.run(fmax=1e-3, steps=100)
```

comments.author: askhl
comments.body:
The diff looks good generally speaking.

I would also be fine with applying this to other files.

comments.author: ajjackson

It seemed a good time to try it: now we are on Py 3.10 we can replace Union with | 😁
